reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a compensation plan that asks viewers to pay a $99 membership fee and buy mining-pool shares while describing daily profit participation. It also ties recruiting members and their purchases or cycle activity to referral commissions, team bonuses, and matching payments, and urges viewers to join through provided contact and registration directions. the available video evidence does not establish whether the mining or payments occurred or verify the linked destination.

citations.quote: On your next third, fourth and fifth person you personally enroll will be placed on Team Number Two.
You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase. This is paid of full and partial shares from the mining pools. You also earn an additional 5% bonus in their first two personally enrolled people.
In the first mining pool, you pay $500 per share
that pays you for 1,000 days of mining. You receive 50% of the profits

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not promise a fixed dollar return from a mining share. It describes receiving a percentage of profits, with the remainder used to acquire hardware and repurchase shares. That wording ties the amount received to profits rather than establishing that profits will exist. The stated limit of one binary cycle per day also matters: the presentation describes a ceiling on that bonus, not unlimited daily cycles. These terms do not verify the venture, but they leave an important gap in the claim that the viewer is being promised a guaranteed payout.

citations.quote: You receive 50% of the profits and the other 50% will be used to acquire new hardware and repurchase shares into Biclub.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $500 share price establishes a purchase price, not a guaranteed $500 return. Likewise, 'pays you for 1,000 days of mining' describes a stated duration; the accompanying percentage is explicitly a share of profits. The team-placement and commission quotes establish how bonuses are described, but do not establish that any member actually received one.

citations.quote: In the first mining pool, you pay $500 per share that pays you for 1,000 days of mining. You receive 50% of the profits
You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A profit-dependent amount is not the same as a risk warning. The presentation tells viewers they get paid for referring members and for those members' mining-pool purchases. It then sets out commissions on purchases by personally enrolled people and bonuses connected to their recruits. Whether any payment actually occurred is not necessary to recognize what this presentation promotes.

citations.quote: Bitclub pays referral commissions. You get paid for referring new Bitclub members. You get paid when someone you refer buys a share of the mining pools.
You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase. This is paid of full and partial shares from the mining pools. You also earn an additional 5% bonus in their first two personally enrolled people.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this video functions as an explanation of a compensation plan. The presenter announces that subject at the outset, then walks through the conditions for a binary-tree cycle and how successive enrollees are assigned to teams with different percentages. Those are operational details a viewer could examine without accepting the plan's claims. The recruitment language deserves attention, but it should not erase the presentation's substantial explanatory content or turn every account of how a plan operates into proof that its promised payments occur.

citations.quote: Today we will go over the compensation plan for Bitclub Network.
You earn commissions on the Binary Tree when you have 1 person on your left and 1 person on your right.
On your next third, fourth and fifth person you personally enroll will be placed on Team Number Two. You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies prices and team bonuses, but those are also the mechanics the presenter says this presentation will explain. Its quotes establish what the plan claims, not that mining profits or commissions were paid. The cited team placement is a rule being described; on its own, it does not show anyone was placed or paid.

citations.quote: Today we will go over the compensation plan for Bitclub Network.
On your next third, fourth and fifth person you personally enroll will be placed on Team Number Two.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanation is itself promotional. The presenter calls the venture a passive-income referral-based company, tells viewers to get started, and directs those ready to join to make contact. The detailed team rules are framed as earnings the viewer 'will earn,' including bonuses tied to people recruited by enrollees. That is more than a detached operational demonstration, regardless of whether the payments can be independently verified.

citations.quote: It is a cutting-edge, passive income referral-based company that will teach you how to cash in on Bitcoin and other digital currencies.
You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase. This is paid of full and partial shares from the mining pools. You also earn an additional 5% bonus in their first two personally enrolled people.
Get started now. Don't Wait!

opening.argument: Judge, the transaction described here includes a membership and shares in specified mining pools, with stated prices and allocations of mining profits. Referral payments are tied to purchases of those shares, which permits a reading of the commissions as part of a sales program for a stated service. The supplied presentation does not demonstrate that mining was fictitious, that funds were diverted, or that a viewer surrendered credentials. Those absences do not certify the business, but they matter when deciding whether the described commerce itself proves deception.

citations.quote: You pay a one-time membership fee of $99.00. Once your membership is created, you will have 3 mining pools you can engage in.

In the second mining pool, you pay $1,000 per share that pays you for 1000 days of mining. You receive 60% of the profits and the other 40% will be used to acquire new hardware and repurchase shares into Biclub.
You get paid when someone you refer buys a share of the mining pools.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The other side establishes that membership and pool shares cost money and that purchases trigger commissions. It does not establish what happened after purchase, including whether the stated mining service operated. Even the quoted 20% commission is expressed as a percentage of a pool purchase, leaving open the interpretation that a transaction, not recruitment alone, is its immediate basis.

citations.quote: In the first mining pool, you pay $500 per share
You will earn 20% on whatever pool they purchase. This is paid of full and partial shares from the mining pools.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presentation does not stop at commissions on direct sales. It offers earnings when personally enrolled members complete binary cycles and additional bonuses when second-generation members complete them. It also describes percentages on people enrolled by a recruit, continuing 'through Infinity.' An unverified mining service does not make that extensive recruitment-based earnings pitch ordinary commerce.

citations.quote: You also receive an additional $50 each from one of your personal enrollees completes a cycle on the binary. You also receive an additional $ 50 each time one of your second generation members completes a cycle
You also earn an additional 5% bonus in their first two personally enrolled people. This is through Infinity.
